title: A-FIRST Data Science and Analytics for Health Competency Framework

competencies.title: Define and articulate health data literacy in public health
competencies.learning_objective: Define data literacy and core concepts related to health data

competencies.title: Classify health data by structure and functional domain
competencies.learning_objective: Distinguish between the main types of health data

competencies.title: Identify internal and external health data sources and surveillance systems
competencies.learning_objective: Identify typical internal and external data sources used for key public health questions

competencies.title: Explain data governance and stewardship in health systems
competencies.learning_objective: Define data governance and data quality in the public health context

competencies.title: Evaluate consequences and risks of weak governance
competencies.learning_objective: Explain why good data governance and high data quality are essential for sound public health decision-making

competencies.title: Assess public health data across key quality dimensions
competencies.learning_objective: Describe key dimensions of data quality and simple checks that can be used to assess them

competencies.title: Detect governance gaps and quality anomalies in health datasets
competencies.learning_objective: Recognise common governance gaps and data quality issues in small public health datasets

competencies.title: Define data wrangling and contrast raw vs analysis-ready data
competencies.learning_objective: Define data wrangling and its importance in public health data analysis

competencies.title: Sequence and execute the 5 stages of data wrangling
competencies.learning_objective: Explain the core steps in the data wrangling process, from discovery to validation

competencies.title: Apply techniques for handling missing values, duplicates, and outliers
competencies.learning_objective: Describe basic data cleaning techniques and how they improve data quality

competencies.title: Implement reproducible pipelines using scripts, version control, and documentation
competencies.learning_objective: Recognise the importance of reproducible workflows and their role in ensuring transparency and consistency in data analysis

competencies.title: Define the purpose and scope of Exploratory Data Analysis
competencies.learning_objective: Explain what exploratory data analysis (EDA) is and why it is important in public health

competencies.title: Calculate and interpret summary statistics and 2x2 contingency tables
competencies.learning_objective: Describe how to explore single variables and simple relationships between variables using basic summaries and tables

competencies.title: Identify remaining data quality issues and anomalies through EDA summaries
competencies.learning_objective: Explain how EDA can reveal remaining data quality issues and guide further analysis

competencies.title: Interpret simple Python scripts for data wrangling, EDA, and 2x2 tables
competencies.learning_objective: Describe, in simple terms, how Python scripts can be used to carry out basic data wrangling, EDA, and produce summary statistics

competencies.title: Explain cognitive advantages and principles of visual data communication
competencies.learning_objective: Explain why data visualisation is important for public health decisions

competencies.title: Match variables and scale types to visual representations
competencies.learning_objective: Distinguish between different data types

competencies.title: Select appropriate visual formats for specific public health inquiries
competencies.learning_objective: Describe which types of visualisation are appropriate for different data types and public health questions

competencies.title: Audit and interpret charts, detecting misleading scales and distorted axes
competencies.learning_objective: Interpret key messages from these visualisations

competencies.title: Deconstruct time series into level, trend, seasonality, and anomalies
competencies.learning_objective: Explain the importance of time-series analysis in tracking public health trends and interventions

competencies.title: Construct and interpret epidemic curves and surveillance alert thresholds
competencies.learning_objective: Identify key features of time-series data

competencies.title: Structure public health dashboards with KPIs, maps, and interactive filters
competencies.learning_objective: Describe how dashboards combine multiple visualisations to support public health decision-making

competencies.title: Apply usability and ethical design rules to public health dashboards
competencies.learning_objective: Apply best practices in dashboard design to ensure clarity, usability, and ethical data representation

competencies.title: Explain the role and mathematical foundation of Generalized Linear Models
competencies.learning_objective: Define Generalised Linear Models (GLMs) and their role in public health

competencies.title: Distinguish logistic regression (binary) and Poisson regression (counts/rates)
competencies.learning_objective: Distinguish between logistic regression and Poisson regression based on the types of outcomes they model

competencies.title: Interpret Odds Ratios, Relative Risks, and Rate Ratios with confidence intervals
competencies.learning_objective: Explain how GLMs are used to estimate risks, counts, and rates of health events

competencies.title: Formulate GLM specifications for vaccine effectiveness and disease risk analysis
competencies.learning_objective: Identify common public health situations where GLMs support data-driven decisions

competencies.title: Contrast hypothesis-driven statistics with predictive machine learning
competencies.learning_objective: Define Machine Learning and describe how it complements traditional statistical methods in public health

competencies.title: Distinguish supervised classification from regression problem formulations
competencies.learning_objective: Distinguish supervised learning problems as classification or regression tasks, based on the type of outcome

competencies.title: Explain prediction mechanisms of decision trees and random forest ensembles
competencies.learning_objective: Explain in simple terms how decision trees and random forests learn from past data to make predictions

competencies.title: Evaluate overfitting, train/test split, and demographic bias in health AI
competencies.learning_objective: Describe why validation, bias checks, and interpretability are important when applying Machine Learning models in public health

competencies.title: Define NLP and explain its utility for unstructured health narratives
competencies.learning_objective: Define Natural Language Processing (NLP) and describe its role in turning unstructured text into usable data for public health

competencies.title: Sequence text normalization, tokenization, and stop-word removal steps
competencies.learning_objective: Describe a simple NLP pipeline that converts raw text into numerical representations for analysis

competencies.title: Compare Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF numerical text representations
competencies.learning_objective: Distinguish between Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF as basic methods for representing text as numbers

competencies.title: Identify NLP use cases for outbreak signal detection and report summarization
competencies.learning_objective: Identify key public health applications of NLP, including event detection, sentiment monitoring, and report triage
